title: Measurement-bound secret release (DICE-style): seal the SE050 BHK wrap / an extra entropy share to H(DHUK, FSBL-measured secure-image digest) so a modified secure image cannot reconstruct the seed even with full MCU code execution
threat: Malicious or implanted firmware on the MCU after sale (RDP downgrade by glitch, or a pre-sale reflash the user did not SWD-verify) that passes or skips the FSBL fingerprint check: today any code on the die can recompute the DHUK-derived PBS/BHK material and unlock both SEs — the fingerprint is a human-checked indicator, not a cryptographic gate (the Donjon Safe 3 lesson: pairing-secret possession proves access to a secret, not the software running).
proposal: The FSBL (which already holds the verified secure digest `secure_digest` at the branch) hands that digest forward in a typed SRAM handoff block; early secure-world boot derives `seal_key = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, 'pq1-seal-v1' || secure_digest)` and uses it (not plain DHUK) as the wrap key for page 126 (SE050 BHK) and as a third XOR share of the entropy reconstruction (`entropy = half_O ⊕ half_E ⊕ KDF(seal_key)`), or at minimum as the OPTIGA PBS salt derivation input. A legitimate firmware update becomes a journaled re-seal: the OLD image (still running, PIN-unlocked, after CMD_FW_COMMIT verified the new manifest) re-wraps page 126 under the NEW image's signed `secure_hash` from the manifest, exactly like the Phase-B transport→final rotation journal on page 127. The FSBL additionally zeroes the handoff block's SRAM alias before any NS code runs.
rationale: This is the strongest shipped primitive against malicious firmware (Tillitis TKey CDI, DICE/Caliptra): it converts the 8-word fingerprint from 'the user must notice' into 'wrong code cannot unwrap'. It needs no new SE primitive, no classical signer, no new per-signature state, and reuses the existing journal machinery. Because it consumes FSBL bytes (handoff block) and the FSBL freezes at RDP-2, the DECISION must be taken before the #540 cutover even if implementation lands later.
repo_evidence: docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:459 ('No measurement-bound secrets, in any form' — recorded as a current property, not a decision against it)
secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs (grep measure|digest|fingerprint: no hits — PBS/BHK derive from DHUK + persisted salt only)
secure/src/dual_se.rs (grep measure|fsbl|digest: no hits — entropy reconstruction has no measurement input)
fsbl/src/branch.rs:38-98 (handoff carries only MSP/reset vector; the verified `secure_digest` is dropped after render)
secure/src/measured_boot.rs:59-122 (secure world re-measures itself, advisory, compiled out of mode-production per main.rs:256-276)
vendor_precedent: Tillitis TKey (cdi = blake2s(UDS, H(app), USS) — altered app ⇒ different keys); DICE/Caliptra layered CDI. Neither Trezor nor Ledger seal wallet secrets to a firmware measurement (Trezor: 'coreapp can ask for access to raw secrets and will just get them', embed-arch.md:325-326).
risks: Brick class: an interrupted re-seal or a signed-but-buggy update that changes the measured bytes in an unplanned way leaves page 126 unwrappable — mitigated by the page-127 journal pattern and by keeping half_O/half_E unchanged (only the extra share/wrap is sealed; the 24-word mnemonic always recovers). Doubles the update ceremony's state machine (#712/#707 recoverability gates apply). Does not defend against a glitched FSBL that forwards the GENUINE digest while branching to a modified image (BOOT-02 covers that). The P0 is for the owner DECISION (FSBL-byte-affecting); implementation is post-cutover.
